title: Modules — turning services on and off, and configuring them
body:
On the **Modulok** tab you decide which services appear on your site — for example room showcase,
prices, or a booking calendar. The tab has two parts: at the top **„Az én moduljaim”** (what is already
yours), and below it **„Bővítés — amit még hozzáadhat”** (what you can still choose). You can preview
most of them before you decide.

![Screenshot: the Modules tab on a phone](assets/hu/screen.png)

## At the top: what is done, what is missing — the setup cards

At the top of the Modules tab every setup topic is a card, in two groups: **„Ami a foglaláshoz
kell”** (how you rent it out, capacity, prices, calendar, booking rules) and **„Az oldal többi része”**.
The colour of the card's left edge tells you where it stands: green — done; yellow — half done; red — missing;
grey — optional. The card has one sentence about what is there and what is missing — room by room too,
for example “1/3 rooms have a price”.

- The **„Beállítom lépésenként”** button takes you to the topic's questions, the same place as the setup
  that opens on your first login.
- If a topic is waiting for another one, the card shows a padlock and the **„Vár”** label, with what it is
  waiting for below (for example: the prices are needed first). Tapping the card takes you to what has to be done first.
- The **„Végigmegyek lépésenként”** link opens the whole setup, from the beginning.

Below the cards are the list of modules and the expansion section, as before.

## The left-hand menu also shows you what is still missing

On a desktop computer, the list of purchased modules sits under **Modulok** in the left-hand menu. Below
it, after a faint **„Még nem vette meg”** label, come the modules you can still add — each with a round,
blue **+** sign next to it. If you click such a row, the page jumps to that module in the
**„Bővítés — amit még hozzáadhat”** section and highlights it with a frame; adding happens there, with
the usual **„Kosárba teszem”** button. The row itself does not purchase anything. On a phone, this same
list sits behind the **Menü** button. The list is open on the Modules tab and on the modules'
configuration screens; on the other tabs you can expand it with the arrow next to Modules.

## The Modules tab during the free trial

While the free trial is running, the Modules tab **looks different** from what this article describes
below: there is no „My modules” / „Add-ons” split, there are no prices, and you cannot purchase row by
row — during the trial the modules are switched on free of charge, with no subscription to add them to
one by one.

- At the top, the **„Modulok a próbában”** card tells you what is switched on, and that you choose the
  ones you want to keep behind the button; anything you do not choose also stays on until the trial ends.
  If you also received a discount for the trial, the card also states what percentage you get off the
  first fee.
- The **„Megrendelem — csomag és modulok”** button takes you to the same order panel as the „Megrendelem”
  button in the bar at the top of the page: there you choose the package and the modules, and there you
  pay (see the Overview help, „If you continue: continuing means paying”).
- Below it is the list of the switched-on modules. At the end of the row, the **„be”** label shows that
  the module is working now; where a module has its own settings (for example rooms, prices, booking),
  there is also a **„Beállítás”** link — the trial is there precisely so you can fill these in and see
  them on your site.
- If the trial did not start with every module, the card names the trial package, and also says that
  whatever is not included can be added right here.

After payment, the tab switches to the familiar form described below. If you pay during the trial and
did not choose every module, the unchosen ones keep working until the trial ends: in the „My modules”
list, instead of a price, **„próbában ingyen”** appears next to them, and below them the day on which
they will switch off, unless you buy them.

## „How it would look on my site” — take a look before you pay

The button's label depends on where you are standing: in the **„Az én moduljaim”** list it reads
**„Megnézem”**, and on the **„Bővítés”** cards **„Megnézem az oldalamon”**. Both do the same thing:
your own website opens the way it would look with that module, with the relevant section highlighted. At
the top you can switch between the **„Mobil”** and **„Asztali”** view, and with the **„Teljes képernyő”**
button it fills the whole screen. Use the **„Bezárom”** button to step back.

⚠️ **The add-on cards do not always have a button** — and this is intentional. Some modules do not appear
on your site but serve you in another way (for example your own email address is a mailbox service). For
these we do not show a preview in the showcase, because there would be nothing to show. But once you have
bought it, the button is there in the **„Az én moduljaim”** row — even if the module has no section of
its own on the site.

⚠️ **If your website is suspended** (because of an unpaid fee), the button's label everywhere reads
**„Előnézet”** — both for already-purchased modules and on the add-on cards — and the text does not
promise that you can look at it on your own site, because in that case the site is not available to
visitors. What you see is still a real preview; the site is restored once the fee is settled.

This is only a preview: **it does not go live and costs nothing**. The **„Előnézet — még nincs élesítve”**
caption at the top always reminds you of this.

Whatever you have not yet purchased carries a yellow **„MINTA — az Ön adataival töltjük fel”** label on
that section. This means you see the section's layout, but the content will come from your own data — so
you do not mistakenly think this is already your finished page.

## What does a module's row tell you?

Above the list, a sentence sums up how many modules are working properly („**Aktív az oldalán** mind
a … modul”). The rows below it **only state a status when there is something to report** — for example
if you cancelled it, if another module replaces it, if the website is suspended, or if your first fee
will still appear on the next invoice. If nothing appears below a row, that is good news: that module is
working in the usual way.

## Adding and switching off

1. In the **„Bővítés — amit még hozzáadhat”** section, each module is on a card: at the top of the card
   is a reduced image of the section, below it what it gives you and how much it costs. Modules labelled
   **„az árban”** are part of the base fee; for the rest the surcharge is shown — at the same rate at
   which you pay (see the next section).
2. Use the **„Kosárba teszem”** button to put it in your basket. Changed your mind? In the same place is
   the **„Kiveszem a kosárból”** button.
3. What is already yours you can cancel in the **„Az én moduljaim”** section with the **„Kikapcsolom”**
   label. This is **underlined text at the far right of the row**, not a button — deliberately quieter
   than the „Megnézem”/„Beállítás” buttons, but just as much a single click. If you change your mind,
   the **„Mégis megtartom”** label is in the same place. (There is one exception: if the module is
   required by another, live module, cancelling first asks a question — see below,
   *„When a module comes together with another module”*.)
4. The buttons here do **not go live** yet: everything is collected in the **basket**. While the basket
   is empty, it is nowhere to be seen. As soon as you put something in it, **on a phone** a dark basket
   button appears at the bottom right — showing the number of items, and for a paid module also the
   amount to pay now — and if you tap it, the basket slides up from the bottom (the **×** at the top
   right closes it). **On a desktop computer** the basket sits next to the showcase, on the right, and
   stays in place as you scroll. The basket shows, row by row, what would switch on and what would be
   cancelled, below it the **„Fizetendő most:”** total and the **„Következő számla így:”** row — from
   which you can see what your next invoice will be.
5. The **„Tovább a fizetéshez”** button finalises everything at once; for a paid add-on a confirmation
   card opens first (see below). If the basket contains only free changes (for example a cancellation),
   the button's label is **„Alkalmazom a módosításokat”**, and the change takes effect immediately. The
   **„Kiürítem a kosarat”** button resets everything.

## Hiding from guests — the „Látható / Nem látható” (visible / hidden) switch

If you only want to stop showing a module for a while — for example, you don't want your prices to show
in winter, or you are taking new photos —, **you don't need to cancel it**. In the **„Az én moduljaim”**
(my modules) part, the row of every module that has its own place on your website has a switch:

- **„Látható”** (visible, green) — the module is on your website.
- **„Nem látható”** (hidden, grey) — the module's section and its menu item disappear from your website.

One tap on the switch, and the change applies on your website **straight away** — it doesn't go into the
basket, there is no payment and no confirmation. A short sentence in the tapped row confirms what
happened. Switching back works the same way, with one tap.

![The module list: Photos hidden, Rooms and Online booking visible](assets/hu/lathatosag.png)

**How is this different from cancelling?** Hiding only changes what the guest sees:

- the module's **fee stays** — it appears on your invoice just as before;
- its **settings are kept**, and with the **„Beállítás”** (Setting) button you can edit them while it is hidden, too;
- once switched back, everything appears exactly as it was.

If you won't need the module for a longer time, cancel it with the **„Kikapcsolom”** (turn off) label
(see above) — that is what ends the fee. Under the row of a hidden module it says:
**„Rejtve a vendég elől — az előfizetése és a beállításai megmaradnak.”** (hidden from guests — your
subscription and settings are kept).

**Good to know:**

- The **Időpontkérés, kapcsolat** (Booking request, contact) module can't be hidden; its row says
  **„Mindig látszik”** (always visible): this is how guests get in touch with you, so your website can't
  do without it. If **Online foglalás** (Online booking) is yours as well, the booking request row has no
  switch — the booking calendar takes its place (see the picture).
- There is no switch for modules that don't appear on the website (for example your own e-mail address),
  or for one-off services (for example the multilingual website), either.
- If you hide **Árak, szezonok** (Prices, seasons) while **Online foglalás** is visible, the booking
  calendar **shows no prices** — the guest asks for a quote, and you reply to it. The booking row tells
  you so with this sentence: **„Árat nem mutat, mert az Árak rejtve van.”** (shows no prices, because
  Prices is hidden).
- If you hide **Online foglalás**, the **booking request form** appears in its place, so the guest can
  still write to you.
- If you hide **Képek a szállásról** (Photos of the accommodation), the gallery disappears, but the main
  photo at the top of the page stays.
- If you later cancel a hidden module and then buy it again, it will be **visible** again.
- While your website is suspended, the switches don't appear.
- **During the free trial**, too, you can hide modules the same way in the **„Modulok a próbában”**
  (modules in the trial) list: there is no fee and no **„Kikapcsolom”** there, and under the name of a
  hidden module it briefly says **„Rejtve a vendég elől”** (hidden from guests).

## When a module comes together with another module

Some modules can only work together with another one — for example because they build on its data. In
that case the page handles this for you, and always says what it did and why:

- **When you switch one on, the required companion goes into your basket on its own.** Its row (or, for a
  module not yet purchased, its card) is shown marked: next to its name is an **„együtt jár”** label,
  and below it an explanatory line names which module brought it along („… — ehhez jár.”) and why it is
  needed. The companion module's fee counts just the same: the basket and the header total immediately
  show the combined price — even before finalising, as with every other switch.
- **We tell you the moment you click.** If the **„Kosárba teszem”** button also brings along another
  paid module, a short notice appears straight away on the card you clicked: which modules were also
  added to the basket, how much you now pay together, and by how much the monthly fee goes up. Below it,
  the **„Mit miért? — a kosárban”** link opens the basket (on a phone the basket stays closed until then).
- **The basket shows them grouped.** Below the row of your own choice, the **„ehhez jár:”** rows are
  indented — each with its own amount, its monthly price and the sentence explaining why it is needed.
  Below them a summary sentence states the full effect: by how much the monthly fee goes up together,
  and how much you pay now. (For example, „Online foglalás” needs „Árak, szezonok”, which in turn needs
  „Szobák, apartmanok” if there is more than one room.)
- **If you take back what you switched on, the companion it brought along also goes back** — you have
  nothing left to pay for the module that only served the other one. But whatever you yourself also
  ticked, or whatever is an already-paid-for module, naturally stays in place.
- **The required module cannot be switched off on its own while the one that needs it is live.** If you
  still click the **„Kikapcsolom”** label, the page does not carry it out silently but asks a question:
  the pop-up's title states which module prevents switching off, its text explains the reason, and below
  it is an itemised list of which modules and how much fee would be lost if you cancelled them all.
  There are two ways out: the **„Mégsem, marad minden”** button leaves everything unchanged, or the red
  button cancels all the listed modules at once — the button's label states how many modules are
  involved. The pop-up also notes that the cancelled modules stay live until the end of the paid period,
  their content is kept, and they can be switched back on at any time.

So the pop-up is **an offer, not an execution**: it never cancels anything on its own — „cancelling
together” only happens if you explicitly ask for it with the red button.

## How much does it cost? — prices follow the rate at which you pay

Every paid module has a price label next to it. What it says depends on whether you chose **monthly or
annual payment**. You can read this off above, in the **„Előfizetés”** box on the **„Jelenlegi díj”**
field: if it ends in „/hó”, your payment is monthly; if „/év”, then annual.

- **With monthly payment** the label is simply the monthly surcharge, for example „490 Ft/hó”.
- **With annual payment** the label states both, and **the annual amount comes first, in larger type**:
  „4 900 Ft/év”, with „490 Ft/hó” faintly below it. The number in front is what you actually pay; the
  monthly one stays there because it lets you compare modules with one another.

In the **„Az én moduljaim”** list, that is, for modules you have already purchased, **there is no „+”
sign before the price** — the amount shown there is not an item to be added but what you already pay for
them. The „+” sign appears only on the cards in the **„Bővítés — amit még hozzáadhat”** section, because
there it really is an increase.

![A module's price label with annual payment](assets/hu/arcimke.png)

The annual amount is less than twelve times the monthly one because with annual payment you get **a few
months as a gift** — exactly how many we always state below the summary (further down, in the summary
image, two months for example). This way you can see at a glance how much your next annual invoice goes
up by if you switch the module on.

This figure is about how much your **next** annual fee will be. How much we deduct now, when you switch
it on, is different — it is pro-rated, and the *„When do you pay for the new module?”* section below tells
you.

### At the end of the list is the total

Below the **„Az én moduljaim”** list, three boxes sum up what you pay:

![The modules' summary with annual payment](assets/hu/arak.png)

- **„Modulok együtt”** — the fee for the purchased modules together, with the number in brackets. This
  figure means the **billed** modules: the ones you actually pay for.
- **„Alapdíj (honlap + időpontkérés)”** — the package's base fee, which always applies. If you switched
  on the **„Online foglalás”** module, it takes over the place of the enquiry form on the site, so this
  label then changes to **„Alapdíj (honlap + kapcsolatfelvétel)”**: the base fee still includes the
  guest being able to reach you, just not via the enquiry form. (In the **„Az én moduljaim”** list the
  Enquiry row still stays there in that case too, and states what stands in its place.)
- **„Éves díja összesen”** (with monthly payment **„Havi díja összesen”**) — **this is what you actually
  pay**, which is why this box is the highlighted one. Below all three boxes the smaller figure also
  appears in the same breakdown, so that the three boxes can be compared.

> **The three boxes also add up.** The two left-hand boxes give the far-right one — both in the large
> figures and in the monthly breakdown below them. With annual payment, next to the monthly fee is also
> the multiplier (how many months we bill), because in that case we do not bill twelve monthly fees but
> fewer: the difference is the gift. The multiplier is the same in all three boxes — which is why they
> can be added up.

> **And what does this actually cost per month?** The sentence below the summary states this: there we
> divide the annual fee by twelve, so that figure is smaller than the monthly fee shown in the boxes —
> because the gift months count into it. The two do not contradict each other: the boxes show **what the
> invoice is made up of**, and the sentence shows **how much one month of it is**.

This total is **the same** as what the **„Következő számla”** field of the **„Előfizetés”** box shows
above, and the same as what appears on the label beginning **„Jelenleg”** in the **„Az én moduljaim”**
header — there cannot be two different amounts on the page. The header label is there so you do not have
to scroll through the whole list if you are only interested in today's fee.

> **The switches recalculate it instantly.** If you cancel a module with the **„Kikapcsolom”** label or
> put it in your basket with the **„Kosárba teszem”** button, the total immediately shows the new state —
> in the summary below the list and on the header label beginning **„Jelenleg”** at the same time — even
> before you finalise anything. This way you can see in advance what the decision would mean for your
> invoice.

## When do you pay for the new module?

A paid module **appears on your site after the fee has been paid** — before switching on, a confirmation
card shows item by item what you are buying, for how many months and for how much, and with the
**„Mégsem”** button you can exit it without consequence.

> If you also **cancel** something in the same step, the confirmation card warns you about this
> separately: **„A lemondása ettől függetlenül érvénybe lép — akkor is, ha ez a fizetés nem megy végbe.”**
> The two halves do not share a single fate: the cancellation is locked in when you press the button, the
> purchase only if the payment also succeeds. That is why we tell you **before you click** — afterwards it
> could no longer help with the decision.

- The **first fee is pro-rated**: it covers the (started) months remaining from today until the renewal
  date — with annual payment never more than the number of monthly fees the annual package otherwise
  contains anyway (reduced by the gift months). On the next invoice the module already appears as a
  normal item.
- On the confirmation card, below the items and the **„Fizetendő most”** amount, the next invoice is
  also there, in a row beginning **„Következő számla”**, together with the change — so that before paying
  you can see what your next invoice will be.
- If your **stored card mandate** is active, you choose on the confirmation card: **„A mentett kártyámmal”**
  (instantly, without redirection) or **„Másik kártyával”** (you enter it on the payment provider's page,
  and that becomes the stored card from then on). With the stored card you pay instantly with the button
  beginning **„Terhelés és élesítés”** (the amount is at the end of the label), and the module appears on
  your site straight away. If the bank declines the stored card, **you stay on the Modules tab** — you are
  not taken to an outside payment page — and a red bar tells you what happened (see below: *What if the
  payment fails?*).
- Without a mandate — and if you choose the **„Másik kártyával”** option — the button beginning
  **„Tovább a fizetéshez”** takes you to the payment page; the module goes live when the payment comes
  in. If the payment does not happen, we switch nothing on and charge nothing.

Switching on a **free** module and switching a cancelled module back on remain instant, without payment.

### What if the payment fails?

Two different things can happen, depending on whether you had a stored card mandate. The most common case
**does not even reach the payment page**, so let us start with that.

#### a) The bank declined the stored card — you stay on the Modules tab

In this case the system **does not take you anywhere**: you stay on the same page, and at the top of the
Modules tab a red bar greets you, whose first, bold sentence is
**„A tárolt kártyáját nem sikerült megterhelni.”**. The bar then names which module we did not switch on,
and states that no charge was made either.

What this means — and what is worth knowing, because the bar cannot fit everything:

- **No money moved**, and the module **did not switch on**. There is nothing to „undo”.
- Your **website keeps running unchanged** — a declined add-on charge does not suspend anything, and your
  stored card mandate also stays in place. (This is different from when the *subscription* fee gets
  stuck: that is signalled separately by the Subscription card, under the title „The automatic card
  charge failed”.)
- If you also **cancelled** something in the same step, the bar states this separately: the cancellation
  **took effect**, even though the purchase did not happen.
- In the bar there is a **„Fizetés kézzel”** button, with which you can settle the purchase by card
  payment. ⚠️ This button takes you to the **payment provider's own page**, which looks different from
  the admin interface — this is not an error. ⚠️ The card entered there **does not replace the stored
  mandate**: changing the stored card is a separate path (see the help on the subscription).
- If even the payment link could not be issued, instead of a button this is all that stands there:
  **„Próbálja meg újra, vagy forduljon hozzánk.”** — in that case we do not send you anywhere, because
  there would be nowhere to go.

#### b) You returned from the payment page

Without a mandate (or via manual payment) it is decided on the payment page. The screen always tells you
what happened — and **never leaves you without something to do**:

- „You cancelled the payment” — you stepped back on the payment page (for example because you would
  choose a different package after all). The bar's caption is „Payment cancelled”, the page's first
  highlighted sentence is *„We charged nothing.”* Your order has been kept: with the „Continue the
  payment” button you can continue in the same place.
- „The payment failed” — the bank declined the card. The page's first, highlighted sentence is what
  interests you most in this case: *„No charge was made.”* In other words, money **did not move**, and
  your order was not lost either — you can try again on this same link. On the page is a „Try the payment
  again” button, and below it the exits: back to the admin interface, enter another card, or write to a
  colleague. There is also a **reference identifier** there, copyable with a single tap — **if you write
  to us, please quote this**, because from it we can tell exactly which attempt it is.
- „Successful payment — thank you!”, but the site is not live yet. The charge was made, but we are still
  finalising the site. In this case there is nothing to do: we send the exact address and the login
  details by email, usually within a few hours. Your subscription box is also there on the page — that
  is, you will not learn of your next charge from your bank statement.
- „We cannot find this payment” — this comes up if there is no payment on our side for the link you
  opened: the link is out of date, was interrupted, or did not come from us. ⚠️ **Important, and we write
  this deliberately:** for this link we **cannot tell whether a charge was made** — precisely because we
  do not recognise it. We do not reassure you with „we did not charge”, nor frighten you with „failed”:
  both would be guesswork. If you want to be sure, check the charge **on your bank's statement**. From
  the page you can step back to the home page, and you can write to us too.

If after the payment you stay on the „processing” screen, it refreshes on its own. If in the meantime we
did not reach the payment provider, the page states this too — in that case what you see is **our
records**, not the bank's final answer.

> These screens are part of the payment process, so they do not live on the admin interface. We write
> their captions here in quotation marks (not bold) — the help's caption guard measures the bold quotes
> against the admin interface's source, and would wrongly flag a caption living elsewhere as missing.

## What happens when you cancel?

Whatever you cancel **stays active** until the end of the already-paid period (the renewal date) — until
then you see the exact date in the module's row, and with the **„Mégis megtartom”** button you can change
your mind at any time, free of charge. After the renewal date the module comes off the site and off the
invoice too.

⚠️ **If you swap in one step** (cancel one, buy another), the two halves are not decided together: the
**cancellation locks in immediately**, but the purchase only with the payment. If the payment gets
stuck, the cancellation stays in effect anyway — for now, only the cancellation comes about from the step
intended as a swap. You can change your mind: the **„Mégis megtartom”** button is available until the
renewal date.

There is one exception: if you received a **custom web address** from us, and the commitment period
undertaken for it is still running, your package cannot drop below the minimum fixed at the time of the
commitment. In that case the cancellation does not go through, and a message tells you the minimum —
expanding is still possible at any time in the meantime, and reducing opens up after the commitment
period has elapsed.

## Configuring a module

In the row of a switched-on, configurable module, the **„Beállítás”** button appears — through this you
reach that module's own configuration screen (for example the days of the booking calendar or the prices
of the rooms). A screen is always about one thing, guiding you step by step.

## Why do we „not count” some modules?

If a module is replaced by another (because the two would appear in the same place on the site), the
replaced module is shown with a **„nem számítjuk”** label — in that case you do not pay for it either.
The replaced section **does not appear** on your website: instead, the module that replaced it is shown,
in the same place. The module stays in the list so you can see it is there, it just has no role right now
(and no price). That is why below the list there is a sentence that names all three figures: how many
modules are in the list, how many are live on your site, and how many appear on the invoice. The
sidebar, the **Áttekintés** and the Modules page all show the same „working on your site” figure — the
replaced module is not included in it. And the always-active base module cannot be switched off because
it is through this that guests contact you — without it the site would not bring in enquiries.

## Why is a module not in the Add-ons?

Some modules cannot be ordered for a while (for example the own email address module). These do not
appear among the Add-on cards, but at the bottom of the Add-ons section we write out by name that they
cannot be ordered right now. If you started with a free trial, and these were also included in the trial
package, they were switched on during the trial; but when the trial was continued they switched off,
because they cannot yet be taken on with a subscription. As soon as they can be ordered, you can take
them on right here.

## What is the coupon above the Add-ons?

If you received a coupon or other discount from us, you see it at the top of the **Bővítés** section: how
much the discount is, what it is called and how long it lives. The card always speaks in the discount's
own name:

- the coupon received for your opening subscription appears under the name „kupon”, and the card also
  states that you received this for your opening subscription;
- every other discount in its own name: Egyedi ajánlat, Bemutatkozó ajánlat from the letter, or
  Döntés-segítő ajánlat.

On the showcase cards, in that case the original price appears crossed out, next to it the discounted
price „in the first month” (for an annual account „in the first year”), and below it the ongoing fee:
„utána +490 Ft/hó”. The discount applies only to the first fee — on the next invoice the full monthly
fee already appears, as the basket's „Következő számla így” row also shows. The deduction happens on its
own, you do not need to enter a code.

**Discounts do not add up:** if you are entitled to more than one, the larger one always takes effect.
The smaller one, however, **is not lost**: on a separate line below the card you see that it is kept, and
that this purchase does not use it up — it may still be valid for a later purchase (the line also states
its expiry). If this remaining discount is the opening coupon, you see it on this line under the name
Üdvözlő kedvezmény.

### What do you see after the purchase?

If you bought with a discount, the green confirmation bar writes out not just the total but the full
derivation too: what the fee would have been, how much the discount is (in forints and as a percentage),
and finally — in the **„A kártyáját megterheltük”** row — how much we actually deducted. This way you
can check afterwards too how the figure came about.

⚠️ **The discount is one-off.** That is why at the bottom of the bar it states how much these same
modules cost at the **next renewal**, without a discount — at your account's rate: a monthly fee on a
monthly account, an annual fee on an annual account, exactly the amount with which they appear among the
„Next invoice” items. It is worth keeping an eye on this so that there is no surprise at the next
invoice.

The same goes onto the invoice: the item's name states that it is a discounted price, and in the
invoice's note is the full derivation. The amount to pay is, of course, what we deducted from your card.

If you had no discount, the bar stays the usual single sentence — we do not write out empty discount
lines.
